group.passage: Some of the most useful inventions were never planned. They began when someone noticed something by chance and wanted to know why it happened. The two short texts below tell how the microwave oven and Velcro came into the world.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: The Microwave Oven
passage_parts.text: In the 1940s, an American named Percy Spencer worked at Raytheon, a company that made radar equipment. One day, he was standing next to a machine that produced microwaves for radar. Suddenly, he noticed that the chocolate bar in his pocket had started to melt. Spencer did not know what had caused this, but he wanted to find out. He held a bag of popcorn kernels near the machine, and soon the kernels began to pop. He realized that microwaves could heat food very quickly. In 1945, he and his company asked for a patent for a microwave oven. Their first oven went on sale in 1947. However, it was about six feet tall and very expensive, so few people could have one. It took about twenty years before smaller ovens were ready for home kitchens.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Velcro
passage_parts.text: George de Mestral was an engineer from Switzerland. One day, he went hiking with his dog. When they got home, he found that both his clothes and his dog’s fur were covered with burrs, the seeds of a plant. He wanted to know why they held on so well. Instead of just pulling them off, he looked at one under his microscope. He saw that it was covered with tiny hooks. These hooks could catch on anything with loops, such as cloth or animal fur. De Mestral decided to copy this design. He made one strip of cloth with small hooks and another with tiny loops. His first tries did not work well, but with help from a weaver in France, he finally got it right in 1955. He named his invention Velcro, from two French words meaning “velvet” and “hook.” Today, it can be found on shoes, bags, and even in space.

tags.topic: 意外的發明：微波爐與魔鬼氈

1.explanation_zh: Text A 說 Spencer 站在產生微波的機器旁，口袋裡的巧克力棒 had started to melt（開始融化）。空格前有 had，要接過去分詞（had + p.p.＝已經……），所以把 melt 改成 melted。
evidence: Suddenly, he noticed that the chocolate bar in his pocket had started to melt.
1.strategy_zh: 先用空格句裡的 chocolate bar 回到 Text A 定位原句，再看空格前的 had 決定字形：had 後面一定是過去分詞。
hints: 空格前是 had，這裡要填過去分詞（had + p.p.）。
回到 Text A，找描述巧克力棒發生什麼變化的句子。
原文是 had started to melt；把 melt 改成過去分詞。

2.explanation_zh: Text B 說 de Mestral 沒有直接把芒刺拔掉，而是放在顯微鏡下觀察（looked at one under his microscope），才看見上面布滿小鉤子。空格在 his 後面，要填名詞，原文的 microscope 直接照抄即可。
evidence: Instead of just pulling them off, he looked at one under his microscope.
He saw that it was covered with tiny hooks.
2.strategy_zh: 空格句的 studied a burr under his ___ 對應原文 looked at one under his ___；找到對應句後，確認空格要名詞，就能直接照抄。
hints: his 後面要接名詞：一種能把很小的東西放大來看的工具。
回到 Text B，看 de Mestral 發現 tiny hooks 之前做了什麼。
原文 he looked at one under his ___；這個字可以照抄。

3.explanation_zh: 兩篇都符合的是 B、E。B：Spencer 偶然發現口袋裡的巧克力融化，de Mestral 健行回家後發現衣服和狗毛沾滿芒刺，兩項發明都起於偶然注意到的事。E：Spencer 想查出原因，拿爆米花去試；de Mestral 想知道芒刺為什麼黏得那麼牢，用顯微鏡觀察。A 只符合微波爐，D 只符合 Velcro，C 兩篇都沒提到，F 與兩篇的內容相反。

Suddenly, he noticed that the chocolate bar in his pocket had started to melt.
Spencer did not know what had caused this, but he wanted to find out.
He wanted to know why they held on so well.
Instead of just pulling them off, he looked at one under his microscope.

option_notes_zh.A: 只有 Text A 說第一台微波爐約六呎高又很貴，所以很少人買得起；Text B 沒說 Velcro 一開始太大，只符合一方。
option_notes_zh.C: 兩篇都沒有說發明者在自己的店裡賣；微波爐是由他工作的公司推出上市的。
option_notes_zh.D: 只有 Velcro 的名字來自兩個法文字（velvet、hook），微波爐的名稱由來沒有提到，只符合一方。
option_notes_zh.F: 與兩篇相反：de Mestral 一開始做不好（His first tries did not work well），微波爐也過了約二十年才適合一般家庭。

3.strategy_zh: 「兩篇都符合」題：每個選項都要在 Text A、Text B 各找到一句證據才能選；只在一篇找得到的（只符合一方）、兩篇都沒寫的都不選。
hints: 題目問兩篇「都」符合的敘述，只符合其中一篇的不能選。
比較兩位發明者的經過：一開始怎麼發現的？發現之後做了什麼？
Spencer 用爆米花測試，de Mestral 用顯微鏡觀察，兩人都想弄清楚原因。

A: However, it was about six feet tall and very expensive, so few people could have one.
B: Suddenly, he noticed that the chocolate bar in his pocket had started to melt.
When they got home, he found that both his clothes and his dog’s fur were covered with burrs, the seeds of a plant.
C: In 1945, he and his company asked for a patent for a microwave oven.

D: He named his invention Velcro, from two French words meaning “velvet” and “hook.”
E: Spencer did not know what had caused this, but he wanted to find out.
Instead of just pulling them off, he looked at one under his microscope.

4.explanation_zh: Text A 說第一台微波爐約六呎高，而且 very expensive，所以很少人買得起（few people could have one）。expensive 就是「要花很多錢的、昂貴的」。題目限定形容詞，只寫 expensive，不要連 very 一起抄。
evidence: However, it was about six feet tall and very expensive, so few people could have one.
4.strategy_zh: 依英文定義找字：先確定詞性（adjective），再到指定的短文找和「花很多錢」有關的描述，只寫最精簡的那一個字。
hints: 要找一個形容詞，意思是「要花很多錢的」。
看 Text A 描述第一台微波爐的句子：為什麼很少人能擁有一台？
答案在 about six feet tall and very ___ 這裡，只寫形容詞本身。

translation_zh.text:
【引言】有些最實用的發明從來不是事先計畫好的。它們始於有人偶然注意到某件事，並想知道為什麼會發生。下面兩篇短文介紹微波爐和魔鬼氈（Velcro）是怎麼誕生的。
【A 微波爐】1940 年代，一位名叫珀西．史賓塞（Percy Spencer）的美國人在雷神公司（Raytheon）工作，這家公司生產雷達設備。有一天，他站在一台為雷達產生微波的機器旁邊，突然發現口袋裡的巧克力棒開始融化了。史賓塞不知道是什麼造成的，但他想查個明白。他拿一袋爆米花玉米粒靠近那台機器，玉米粒很快就開始爆開。他明白了微波可以很快地把食物加熱。1945 年，他和公司為微波爐申請了專利。他們的第一台微波爐在 1947 年上市，但它大約有六呎高，而且非常昂貴，所以很少人買得起。又過了大約二十年，體積較小的微波爐才適合放進家庭廚房。
【B 魔鬼氈】喬治．德梅斯特拉爾（George de Mestral）是一位來自瑞士的工程師。有一天，他帶著狗去健行。回到家後，他發現自己的衣服和狗毛上都沾滿了芒刺，也就是某種植物的種子。他想知道它們為什麼黏得這麼牢。他沒有直接把芒刺拔掉，而是拿一個放在顯微鏡下觀察，看到上面布滿細小的鉤子。這些鉤子能鉤住任何有小圈圈的東西，例如布料或動物的毛。德梅斯特拉爾決定模仿這種設計。他做了一條帶有小鉤子的布條，和另一條帶有細小圈圈的布條。他最初的嘗試效果不好，但在一位法國織布師傅的幫忙下，他終於在 1955 年成功了。他把這項發明取名為 Velcro，取自兩個分別意為「天鵝絨」和「鉤子」的法文字。如今，鞋子、包包上都看得到它，甚至連太空中也有。
